experiment.name: Admission phenotype structure, BET cohort
experiment.description: Exploratory phenotype groupings of 148 dogs from admission variables, with stability and null tests; no outcome exists in this dataset and the groups are not subtypes of disease.
experiment.summary: 148 dogs, 22 admission variables: 4 principal axes retained by parallel analysis. Ward clustering chose k = 2 (mean silhouette 0.162; null p = 0.199); mean bootstrap Jaccard 0.89; strongest comparison with the authors' classes is anaemia_class (Cramer's V 0.84, adjusted p < 0.001; circular by construction). Exploratory phenotype groups, no outcome in this dataset.

sections.heading: Question
paragraphs: Do the 148 dogs of the DS05 cohort, all positive for Babesia on PCR (146 of 150 B. rossi only), fall into recognisable admission phenotype groups, or do they form one continuum? And which laboratory and clinical axes carry most of the variance: a regenerative-anaemia axis (haemoglobin, haematocrit, red cell count, reticulocytes), an inflammatory axis (band and segmented neutrophils, monocytes, lymphocytes, platelets) and a protein axis (total protein, albumin)?

sections.heading: What was done
paragraphs: 150 dogs were available; 2 (BET065, BET066) were dropped because more than 30 percent of the 22 input variables were missing, leaving 148. The 22 input variables are the measured numeric and ordinal admission values; calculated indices (mcv, mch, mchc, wcc, arc, globulin) were left out so that no axis is built from a variable and its own parts. 15 skewed non-negative variables were log-transformed (age, duration of illness, rectal temperature, haemoglobin, red cell count, haematocrit, red cell distribution width, segmented neutrophils, band neutrophils, lymphocytes, monocytes, eosinophils, platelet count, nucleated red cells and reticulocytes). All variables were standardised; 41 of 3256 cells (1.3 percent) were filled once by iterative regression imputation, and standardised values were capped at +/-4 for clustering.

Principal component analysis kept 4 axes by parallel analysis (500 permutations; the Kaiser rule would keep 7). Clusters were found with Ward hierarchical clustering on the standardised variables for k = 2 to 8, requiring at least 8 dogs in the smallest cluster; k was the one with the highest mean silhouette. A Gaussian mixture on the principal components, a simulated no-structure null, bootstrap resampling (200 resamples) and repeated 80 percent subsampling (200 subsamples) were used to judge whether the clusters are real. Cluster labels were then compared with the authors' own classes.

sections.heading: Main axes
paragraphs: PC1 (eigenvalue 6.14, 27.9 percent of the variance) is led by haemoglobin, red cell count and haematocrit.
PC2 (eigenvalue 2.31, 10.5 percent of the variance) is led by total serum protein, age and body weight.
PC3 (eigenvalue 1.80, 8.2 percent of the variance) is led by rectal temperature, reticulocytes and pulse rate.
PC4 (eigenvalue 1.56, 7.1 percent of the variance) is led by duration of illness, age and pulse rate.
The 4 retained axes together carry 53.7 percent of the variance.
The red-cell (anaemia) variables load most on PC1 (mean absolute loading 0.33); expected on PC1 - as expected.
The inflammatory / left-shift variables load most on PC2 (mean absolute loading 0.26); expected on PC2 - as expected.
The protein variables load most on PC2 (mean absolute loading 0.25); expected on PC3 - not as expected.

PC1: haemoglobin, red cell count and haematocrit already form one correlation block in the pairwise experiment (EXP01, mean absolute rho 0.76), so this axis largely restates a strong pairwise correlation rather than adding a new relation.

PC2: age and body weight already form one correlation block in the pairwise experiment (EXP01, mean absolute rho 0.41), so this axis largely restates a strong pairwise correlation rather than adding a new relation.
PC3: its leading variables (rectal temperature, reticulocytes and pulse rate) do not sit together in one EXP01 correlation block, so the axis combines relations not seen as a single pairwise block.

sections.heading: Do the dogs form groups?
paragraphs: The chosen number of clusters is k = 2 (highest Ward mean silhouette among admissible k: k = 2: 0.162; k = 3: 0.106; k = 4: 0.109; k = 5: 0.098; k = 6: 0.079). Mean silhouette at k = 2 is 0.162. A silhouette below 0.25 means a continuum rather than separate groups; 0.25 to 0.5 is weak structure.
Cluster sizes: C1 91, C2 57.

Against a no-structure null (simulated Gaussian data with the same correlations, 200 runs), the 95th percentile of the best silhouette is 0.178; the observed best silhouette is 0.162, permutation-style p = 0.199.

Bootstrap stability (Hennig clusterwise Jaccard): C1 mean 0.92 (highly stable); C2 mean 0.87 (highly stable). Guide: below 0.6 unstable, 0.6 to 0.75 a pattern with uncertainty, above 0.75 stable, above 0.85 highly stable. Mean over clusters 0.89.
Consensus over subsamples: mean co-clustering within clusters C1 0.97, C2 0.90, between clusters 0.07; PAC (share of dog pairs with an ambiguous consensus of 0.1 to 0.9) 0.19.
The Gaussian mixture on the principal components prefers k = 2 (diag covariance by BIC), the same k; the two partitions agree with an adjusted Rand index of 0.79.

The high bootstrap Jaccard values do not contradict this: with k = 2 the split falls along the dominant axis and is reproducible, but a reproducible cut through a continuum is not evidence of separate groups.

Negative finding: mean silhouette 0.16 is below 0.25; the silhouette is not better than the null (p = 0.199). The cohort is a continuum along the principal axes, not a set of groups; the clusters are only a convenient partition and should not be read as separate phenotype groups.
What distinguishes each cluster (difference of the cluster median from the other dogs, in robust standard deviations):
C1 (n = 91, median silhouette 0.09): higher reticulocytes (+1.7), lower haemoglobin (-1.7), lower red cell count (-1.7).
C2 (n = 57, median silhouette 0.29): lower reticulocytes (-1.7), higher haemoglobin (+1.7), higher red cell count (+1.7).

sections.heading: Comparison with the authors' classes and co-infection
paragraphs: Cluster labels were cross-tabulated with the authors' derived classes, PCR result for E. canis and the group label. 7 tests were adjusted together with Benjamini-Hochberg.

Circularity: the authors' classes are cut from variables used here (anaemia_class from haematocrit; left_shift from band_neutrophils, seg_neutrophils; habitus_class from habitus_score; illness_class from illness_days; arc_class from arc, not an input). Agreement is therefore expected by construction and is a sanity check, not a discovery.
anaemia_class (n = 148): Cramer's V 0.84 (95 percent interval 0.77 to 0.91), adjusted p < 0.001.
left_shift (n = 148): Cramer's V 0.29 (95 percent interval 0.13 to 0.43), adjusted p = 0.001; De_L_shift merged into L_shft (label 'left shift present').
habitus_class (n = 148): Cramer's V 0.37 (95 percent interval 0.23 to 0.52), adjusted p < 0.001.
illness_class (n = 148): Cramer's V 0.16 (95 percent interval 0.04 to 0.31), adjusted p = 0.204.
arc_class (n = 148): Cramer's V 0.49 (95 percent interval 0.37 to 0.62), adjusted p < 0.001.
pcr_e_canis: too few dogs to test (minority levels have 3 dogs); the table is descriptive only (n = 148).
group_label: too few dogs to test (minority levels have 1, 3 dogs); the table is descriptive only (n = 148).

sections.heading: Robustness to missing data
paragraphs: Each sensitivity analysis repeats the standardisation, clustering and k choice with one change and compares the result with the main partition on the dogs they share (adjusted Rand index, ARI) and compares the first three principal axes with the main ones (Tucker congruence, 1 = identical; axes compared in order, shared variables only).
S1_complete_case (n = 113): chosen k = 2, silhouette 0.176, ARI with main 0.90, Tucker PC1 to PC3 1.00, 0.94, 0.84.
S2_median_imputation (n = 148): chosen k = 2, silhouette 0.160, ARI with main 1.00, Tucker PC1 to PC3 1.00, 1.00, 1.00.
S3_drop_respiratory_rate_temperature (n = 148): chosen k = 2, silhouette 0.175, ARI with main 0.92, Tucker PC1 to PC3 1.00, 1.00, 0.94.
S4_add_derived_back (n = 148): chosen k = 2, silhouette 0.130, ARI with main 0.77, Tucker PC1 to PC3 1.00, 0.86, 0.73.
S5_no_log_transform (n = 148): chosen k = 4, silhouette 0.134, ARI with main 0.61, Tucker PC1 to PC3 1.00, 0.90, 0.96.
The partition is robust by the pre-set rule: complete-case and median-imputation analyses each give the same k or an ARI of at least 0.6 with the main partition.

sections.heading: Limits
paragraphs: 148 dogs and 22 correlated variables: the analysis is exploratory. Clusters are phenotype groupings of admission values; the dataset has no outcome, so nothing here is prognostic and nothing is meant for clinical use.
One hospital cohort, B. rossi in 146 of 150 dogs. The 3 E. canis co-infected dogs and the 1 B. vogeli dog support counts only; no tests.
Values are from a single admission, so group membership says nothing about the course of disease.

Missing values were filled once before resampling, so stability is optimistic for the variables with the most gaps (respiratory rate and temperature). Ordinal scores (lymph node score, habitus score) were treated as numbers.
Entry or unit errors in the raw sheet can drive an axis; atypical dogs are handled in a separate experiment (EXP06) and checked against the raw sheet.
UMAP was not available, so the figure coordinates are the first two principal components; they feed no statistic.

imputation.method: IterativeImputer(BayesianRidge, max_iter=20, sample_posterior=False, initial_strategy=median), once on the standardised matrix before resampling; matrix re-standardised afterwards

notes: Ordinal variables (lymph_node_score, habitus_score) treated as numeric.
Calculated variables (mcv, mch, mchc, wcc, arc, globulin) carry derived_from and are excluded from clustering; sensitivity S4 adds them back.
Clipping at +/-4 SD applies to the clustering matrix only; PCA and factor analysis use the unclipped standardised matrix.
Ward partition computed with scikit-learn AgglomerativeClustering; resampling uses scipy Ward linkage (same algorithm, ARI between them = 1.000).
Variables with zero MAD cannot enter the 'distinguishing' list: eosinophils
Chosen-k Jaccard and consensus use imputed-once data; stability is optimistic for the most-imputed variables.
